theme: Asking a coworker for a favor
summary_zh: 學會用委婉句型請同事幫忙：說明原因、讓對方容易答應，也容易拒絕。

vocab.zh: 忙翻了、事情多到做不完
vocab.definition: having so much work that you can hardly deal with it
vocab.example: I'm completely swamped this week, so can we meet on Monday?
vocab.example_zh: 我這週忙翻了，我們可以星期一再約嗎？

vocab.zh: 代班、暫時接手（某人的工作）
vocab.definition: to do someone's work for them while they are away
vocab.example: Could you cover for me at the meeting on Friday?
vocab.example_zh: 週五的會議你可以幫我代一下嗎？

vocab.definition: a warning or piece of information given in advance
vocab.example: Thanks for the heads-up about the office move.
vocab.example_zh: 謝謝你先提醒我辦公室要搬家。

vocab.definition: to look at or explain something carefully from beginning to end
vocab.example: Let's go through the contract together before we sign it.
vocab.example_zh: 簽約前我們一起把合約仔細看過一遍吧。

vocab.definition: to learn the latest information about something so you can work on it
vocab.example: It took me a week to get up to speed on the new project.
vocab.example_zh: 我花了一週才進入新專案的狀況。

vocab.zh: 把（某人）加進討論、讓某人知情
vocab.definition: to include someone in a conversation or email so they know what is happening
vocab.example: I'll loop in Jenny so she knows what we decided.
vocab.example_zh: 我會把 Jenny 加進來，讓她知道我們的決定。

vocab.definition: used to tell someone they do not need to do something quickly
vocab.example: Send it whenever you can. No rush.
vocab.example_zh: 你方便的時候再寄就好，不急。

vocab.definition: used to thank someone and say you will help them in return later
vocab.example: Thanks for staying late. I owe you one!
vocab.example_zh: 謝謝你留下來加班，欠你一次！

reading.title: How to Ask for Help Without Feeling Awkward
paragraphs: Many people find it harder to ask for help than to give it. We worry that we will look weak, or that we are interrupting someone who is already swamped. As a result, we either struggle alone or send a short, slightly demanding message like "Can you check this today?"
Research on workplace behavior suggests that people are much more willing to help than we expect. The key is to make the request easy to say yes to, and just as easy to say no to.

Start by giving a reason. "I was wondering if you could look at my slides, because you know the client better than I do" explains why you chose this person. Then be specific about what you need and when. "Would it be possible to go through the numbers with you for ten minutes before Thursday?" is much easier to answer than a vague "Can you help me with the report?"

It also helps to offer flexibility. Adding "no rush" or "only if you have time" shows that you respect the other person's workload. If you are asking someone to cover for you while you are away, give them a heads-up as early as possible and leave clear notes so they can get up to speed quickly. Remember to loop in anyone else who needs to know about the arrangement.

Finally, close the loop. Thank the person afterward and tell them how things turned out. A simple "Thanks so much, I owe you one" goes a long way, and it makes the next request far less awkward, for both of you.

questions.q: According to the article, what do people often get wrong about asking for help?
options: They think others are less willing to help than they really are.
They ask for help too often.
They ask the wrong people for help.
They give too many reasons for their requests.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：people are much more willing to help than we expect，別人其實比我們以為的更願意幫忙。

questions.q: Why is "Would it be possible to go through the numbers with you for ten minutes before Thursday?" a better request?
options: It sounds more urgent.
It is specific about what is needed and when.
It avoids giving a reason.
It asks the person to do all the work.
questions.explain_zh: 第三段：be specific about what you need and when，時間、內容都講清楚，比含糊的請求好回答。

questions.q: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: Saying thank you is only necessary for big favors.
Thanking people properly makes future cooperation easier.
You should always repay a favor immediately.
Most people forget the favors they have done.
questions.explain_zh: 最後一段：好好道謝 makes the next request far less awkward，暗示道謝能讓之後的合作更順，這題考推論。

grammar.point: Polite requests: I was wondering if… / Would it be possible to…
grammar.point_zh: 委婉請求：I was wondering if… ／ Would it be possible to…
grammar.explain_zh: 英文用「過去進行式」和 would、could 讓請求聽起來更客氣，也給對方拒絕的空間。I was wondering if 後面接完整子句（you could + 原形動詞）；Would it be possible to 後面接原形動詞；Would you mind 後面接 V-ing。請同事或主管幫忙時，比直接說 Can you… 更得體。
grammar.pattern: I was wondering if + you/we could + V ／ Would it be possible to + V ／ Would you mind + V-ing

examples.en: I was wondering if you could cover for me on Friday afternoon.
examples.zh: 不知道你週五下午能不能幫我代班。

examples.en: Would it be possible to get the file by Wednesday?
examples.zh: 請問星期三前可以拿到檔案嗎？

examples.en: Would you mind looping in the finance team?
examples.zh: 可以麻煩你把財務團隊加進來嗎？

exercises.q: I was wondering ___ you could take a quick look at my proposal.
exercises.explain_zh: I was wondering 後面用 if 或 whether 帶出一個子句。

exercises.q: Would you mind ___ me the meeting notes?
options: send
to send
sending
sent
exercises.explain_zh: Would you mind 後面接 V-ing：Would you mind sending…?

exercises.q: Would it be possible ___ (borrow) your charger for an hour?
exercises.explain_zh: Would it be possible + to + 原形動詞。

exercises.q: Which request sounds the most polite when asking a busy colleague for help?
options: Check my report today.
I was wondering if you could check my report when you have a minute.
You have to check my report.
Why don't you check my report now?
exercises.explain_zh: I was wondering if you could… 加上 when you have a minute，語氣最委婉、也尊重對方時間。

exercises.q: Your coworker asks, "Would you mind covering for me tomorrow?" You are happy to help. What do you say?
options: Yes, I would.
Yes, I mind.
No, not at all.
No, I wouldn't help.
exercises.explain_zh: mind 是「介意」。回答 No, not at all（一點也不介意）才是「可以」。

listening.title: Amy asks Ben to cover for her

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Amy
lines.text: Hey Ben, sorry to bother you. Do you have a minute?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ben
lines.text: Sure, what's up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Amy
lines.text: I have a doctor's appointment next Tuesday morning. I was wondering if you could cover for me at the client call.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ben
lines.text: Next Tuesday? Hmm, I'm pretty swamped that week, but the call is only half an hour, right?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Amy
lines.text: Yes, thirty minutes at most. It's mostly a progress check. I'll send you my notes so you can get up to speed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ben
lines.text: Okay, that sounds doable. Would it be possible to go through the notes together on Monday?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Amy
lines.text: Of course. How about Monday at four? And I'll loop in the client so they know you're joining.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ben
lines.text: Perfect. Thanks for the heads-up, by the way. It's much easier when I know a week in advance.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Amy
lines.text: Thank you so much, Ben. I owe you one.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Ben
lines.text: Don't worry about it. Just bring me a coffee on Monday.

questions.q: Why does Amy need Ben to cover for her?
options: She is going on vacation.
She has a doctor's appointment.
She has another client meeting.
She is working from home.
questions.explain_zh: Amy：I have a doctor's appointment next Tuesday morning.

questions.q: What does Ben ask for before agreeing completely?
options: To go through Amy's notes together on Monday
To move the client call to Wednesday
To make the call shorter
To get help with his own work
questions.explain_zh: Ben：Would it be possible to go through the notes together on Monday?

questions.q: What can we infer about Ben's attitude?
options: He is annoyed that Amy asked him.
He is willing to help, partly because Amy asked early.
He wants Amy to pay him back with extra work.
He doesn't think the call is important.
questions.explain_zh: Ben 雖然很忙但還是答應，並說 It's much easier when I know a week in advance，可推論他願意幫忙，部分是因為 Amy 提早說。

dictation: I was wondering if you could cover for me at the client call.
I'll send you my notes so you can get up to speed.
Thanks for the heads-up, by the way.

shadowing: Sorry to bother you. Do you have a minute?
I was wondering if you could cover for me on Friday.
Would it be possible to go through it together tomorrow?
Thank you so much. I owe you one.

prompts.question: You need a colleague to check your presentation before an important meeting. Ask them politely. Give a reason and say when you need it.
prompts.question_zh: 重要會議前，你需要同事幫你看一下簡報。請有禮貌地拜託對方，說明原因和需要的時間。
hints: Request: I was wondering if you could…
Reason and time: because… / by Thursday / no rush if…
prompts.sample: Hi Jason, sorry to bother you. I was wondering if you could take a quick look at my slides for Thursday's meeting. You've worked with this client before, so I'd really value your opinion. Would it be possible to get your comments by Wednesday afternoon? If you're too busy, no worries at all.

prompts.question: Talk about a time a coworker helped you. What did they do, and how did you thank them?
prompts.question_zh: 說說同事曾經幫你的一次經驗。他們做了什麼？你怎麼道謝？
hints: Help: She helped me get up to speed on…
Thanks: I bought her lunch / told our manager…
prompts.sample: When I first joined my company, I didn't understand our reporting system at all. A senior colleague spent two lunch breaks showing me how everything worked, and she helped me get up to speed really quickly. To thank her, I bought her a nice lunch and told our manager how helpful she had been.

writing.task: Write a short message to your colleague, Kelly. You will be on leave next Thursday and Friday. Ask her politely to cover for you on one task, explain what she needs to do, and thank her.
writing.task_zh: 寫一則訊息給同事 Kelly：你下週四、五請假，請她幫你代理一項工作，說明她要做什麼，並向她道謝。
writing.sample:
Hi Kelly,

Just a heads-up: I'll be on leave next Thursday and Friday. I was wondering if you could cover for me on the weekly sales report while I'm away. It usually takes about an hour. You just need to update the numbers in the shared spreadsheet and send it to Mark by 5 p.m. on Friday.

I'll leave detailed notes in the folder, but would it be possible to spend ten minutes going through them together on Wednesday? That way you can get up to speed quickly.

If you're too busy, no problem at all — just let me know. Thanks so much, I owe you one!

Best,
Mimi
checklist_zh: 開頭先給對方預告（Just a heads-up…）
用 I was wondering if… 委婉提出請求
清楚說明要做什麼、什麼時候完成
給對方拒絕的空間（If you're too busy…）
結尾道謝（Thanks so much / I owe you one）

translation.zh: 不知道你下週二能不能幫我代班？
translation.en: I was wondering if you could cover for me next Tuesday.
alt: I was wondering whether you could cover for me next Tuesday.

translation.zh: 請問星期五前可以把報告寄給我嗎？不急。
translation.en: Would it be possible to send me the report by Friday? No rush.
alt: Would it be possible for you to send me the report by Friday? There's no rush.

translation.zh: 謝謝你先提醒我，欠你一次！
translation.en: Thanks for the heads-up. I owe you one!
alt: Thanks for letting me know in advance. I owe you one!

reading.title: The Hidden Economy of Office Favors
paragraphs: Every workplace runs on two systems. One is official: job descriptions, org charts and approval processes. The other is unofficial, and arguably more powerful: a constant exchange of small favors. Someone covers a shift, shares a template, or puts in a good word with a manager, and an invisible balance sheet quietly updates.

Most of the time, this unwritten economy works remarkably well. It lets people cut through red tape and get things done without filing a ticket for every minor request. But it has its pitfalls. Some people end up doing far more than their share, simply because they find it hard to say no. Others become known for always asking and never offering, and goodwill toward them gradually dries up.

The way a favor is requested shapes how it is received. A request that comes out of the blue, with no context and an unreasonable deadline, puts the other person on the spot. They may agree, but they are unlikely to feel good about it. By contrast, a request that acknowledges the other person's workload, explains why their help matters, and leaves a genuine way out tends to be met with enthusiasm rather than resentment.

Interestingly, the people who are best at asking for help are often the ones who give it most freely. Having helped others, they have built up a reserve of trust, and they understand what it feels like to be on the receiving end of a badly timed request.
In the end, none of this needs to be calculated or transactional. Paying attention to timing, tone and gratitude is simply a way of showing that you value your colleagues' time as much as your own.

questions.q: What does the writer mean by an "invisible balance sheet"?
options: A secret budget that managers keep
An unspoken record of who has helped whom
A list of tasks people have not finished
The company's official financial report
questions.explain_zh: 第一段把同事間互相幫忙比喻成帳本：每幫一次忙，這本「看不見的帳」就會更新，指的是誰幫過誰的心照不宣紀錄。這題考推論。

questions.q: According to the article, what happens to people who always ask but never offer help?
options: They are promoted more quickly.
Their colleagues gradually become less willing to help them.
They are given fewer tasks.
They learn to say no more often.
questions.explain_zh: 第二段：goodwill towards them gradually dries up，大家對他們的善意慢慢消失。

questions.q: Why are people who help others often good at asking for help, according to the writer?
options: They have more free time.
They know which managers to ask.
They have built up trust and understand the helper's point of view.
They usually have more senior positions.
questions.explain_zh: 第四段：they have built up a reserve of trust, and they understand what it feels like to be on the receiving end…

questions.q: What can we infer about the writer's view in the final paragraph?
options: Favors should be carefully counted to keep things fair.
Good habits around favors come from respect, not from calculation.
Asking for favors should be avoided whenever possible.
Only managers need to worry about how favors are requested.
questions.explain_zh: 最後一段說 None of this needs to be calculated or transactional，重點是 valuing your colleagues' time，可推論作者認為出發點是尊重而不是算計。

listening.title: A last-minute favor

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Hey, Nina, sorry, I know you're slammed, but could I steal you for literally two minutes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Uh, sure, as long as it really is two minutes. What's up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: So, the board pack for tomorrow. My numbers for the Asia region don't add up, and I can't for the life of me figure out why.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Tomorrow? Ryan, it's half past five.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: I know, I know. I should've flagged it this morning. I was wondering if you could just glance at the formulas, since you built the original model.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Okay, look, I've got a call at six that I really can't move. Would it be possible to send it over now? I'll take a look right after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: That would be amazing. Honestly, if you can't, just say, and I'll hunt down someone from finance.

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: No, it's fine, it's probably a broken link to last quarter's sheet. That happens all the time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: You're a lifesaver. Should I loop in Mark, or...?

lines.speaker: B
lines.name: Nina
lines.text: Let's not worry him yet. If it's what I think it is, it's a five-minute fix. Just, you know, next time, give me a bit more notice?

lines.speaker: A
lines.name: Ryan
lines.text: Absolutely. Lunch is on me this week.

questions.q: Why does Ryan ask Nina in particular for help?
options: She is his manager.
She built the original model.
She works in the finance team.
She prepared the Asia figures.
questions.explain_zh: Ryan：since you built the original model，因為原本的模型是 Nina 做的。

questions.q: When will Nina look at the file?
options: Immediately, before her call
Right after her six o'clock call
Tomorrow morning
After she talks to Mark
questions.explain_zh: Nina：I've got a call at six… I'll take a look straight after。

questions.q: What can we infer about how Nina feels about the request?
options: She is delighted to help at any time.
She is willing to help but a little frustrated by the late notice.
She refuses because she is too busy.
She thinks Ryan should ask the finance team instead.
questions.explain_zh: 她答應幫忙，但先說 it's half past five，最後又說 next time, give me a bit more notice?，可推論她願意幫但對臨時通知有點無奈。

dictation: I know you're slammed, but could I steal you for literally two minutes?
I can't for the life of me figure out why.
Would it be possible to send it over now?

in a difficult situation where you have to answer or act immediately
used to say you cannot do something however hard you try
